stories.title: Stanford Crossing Offers 100 Acres for Development in Fast-Growing Lathrop
stories.excerpt: Stanford Crossing is positioning more than 100 acres of commercial land within Lathrop, representing what it calls a rare opportunity for developers to establish an early foothold in a rapidly growing market. The mixed-use development offers lot sizes ranging from 1/2 acre to 40 acres for retail, dining and service offerings and is located along Interstate 5 between Lathrop Rd./Spartan Way and River Islands Pkwy./Loise Ave. exits, providing high visibility and easy access for future customers. As one of Northern California’s fastest-growing communities, Lathrop is entering its next phase of growth. The city has pursued a deliberate strategy to attract new residents, businesses and investments. “Lathrop’s growth story isn’t the result of a temporary spike—it’s the outcome of years of strategic planning and investment,” said Jeff Wilson, co-managing partner, Saybrook Fund Advisors. “Stanford Crossing is seeing significant opportunities for commercial developers and retailers looking for a market with compelling momentum.” The post Stanford Crossing Offers 100 Acres for Development in Fast-Growing Lathrop appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stanford Crossing offering 100+ acres in Lathrop, CA for mixed-use development.
Lathrop positioned as Northern California's fastest-growing community with strategic growth plan.
Land parcels range 0.5 to 40 acres; I-5 corridor location provides high visibility.
stories.summary: Stanford Crossing is marketing over 100 acres of commercial land in Lathrop, California—one of Northern California's fastest-growing communities—with lot sizes from half an acre to 40 acres positioned along I-5 between major exits. The development strategy reflects years of deliberate city planning to attract residents, businesses, and investment. The high-visibility, high-access location signals momentum for commercial and retail developers entering an early-phase growth market.
stories.impact: Lathrop's strategic growth and land availability create a window for multifamily developers to acquire and entitle residential product ahead of population influx from the Central Valley region. Early-stage market entry before major institutional competition could secure advantageous land costs and entitlements; monitor for employer announcements, job growth data, and demographic migration patterns to Lathrop to time development pipeline.

stories.title: Grand Peaks, PCCP Acquire Mixed-Use Multifamily in Beaverton
stories.excerpt: Multifamily real estate investment firm Grand Peaks, in partnership with PCCP, LLC, announced the acquisition of West End District, a 424-unit, mixed-use multifamily community located in the heart of Beaverton, Oregon. Completed in 2021-2022, the property pairs contemporary apartment homes with approximately 34,262 square feet of ground-floor retail. The retail component anchors the property as a neighborhood destination, providing residents and the surrounding Beaverton community with convenient access to shops, dining and services just steps from home. CBRE served as the sales and debt broker on the transaction, with financing provided through Freddie Mac. Greystar will serve as the property manager for the community. The acquisition expands Grand Peaks’ presence in the Pacific Northwest. The addition of the West End District brings Grand Peaks’ diversified portfolio to approximately 11,000 apartment homes nationwide. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post Grand Peaks, PCCP Acquire Mixed-Use Multifamily in Beaverton appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Grand Peaks and PCCP acquire 424-unit West End District in Beaverton, Oregon (2021-2022).
Property includes 34,262 sq ft ground-floor retail; Freddie Mac financing and Greystar management.
Expands Grand Peaks portfolio to ~11,000 units nationally; strengthens Pacific Northwest presence.
stories.summary: Grand Peaks and PCCP acquired West End District, a 424-unit mixed-use multifamily community completed in 2021–2022 in Beaverton, Oregon, with 34,262 square feet of ground-floor retail. Freddie Mac provided financing and Greystar took on property management. The transaction marks Grand Peaks' strategic expansion in the Pacific Northwest, bringing its national portfolio to approximately 11,000 units.
stories.impact: Institutional capital continuing to acquire stabilized, mixed-use multifamily assets in mid-size Pacific Northwest markets signals sustained confidence in Beaverton's rental fundamentals and retail-anchored value-add profile. For developers, this indicates strong exit appetite for newly stabilized Class A product with retail components; refinance availability (Freddie Mac) remains accessible for quality assets in secondary West Coast metros.

stories.title: Azimuth Sells Bronx Educational Facility to Equality Charter School for $55M
stories.excerpt: Azimuth Development Group has handed over ownership of a school facility in the East Bronx that appears to have been a build-to-suit construction job for the firm. Azimuth President Guido Subotovsky signed a $54.5 million deed transfer of 801 Bartholdi Street to Equality Charter School, a tuition-free public school that will use the property as a 63,000-square-foot elementary school, according to property records. The property appears to have been completed in 2025 and contains two cafeterias, a gymnasium, and 6,000 square feet of recreational space on the rooftop. The site can accommodate 900 students, according to Azimuth’s website. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. Spokespeople for Azimuth and Equality Charter School did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Equality Charter School currently has an elementary school at 3901 White Plains Road, a middle school at 4140 Hutchinson River Parkway East, and a high school at 2141 Seward Avenue, all in the Bronx. It’s unclear if the school’s administration will be consolidating any of its existing facilities within the new Bartholdi Street location. Azimuth, founded in 2009 by Subotovsky, specializes in projects that benefit local communities such as the development of affordable housing as well as market-rate units. The company says it has built over 1 million square feet of mixed-use developments in the five boroughs since it was founded. In terms of educational facilities, Azimuth has previously teamed up with Joy Construction in the $140 million mixed-income development of two buildings and 330 rental units 2069 Bruckner Boulevard. It leased 12,000 square feet in that development to The Village School in June 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Azimuth Development sold 63,000 sq ft educational facility (801 Bartholdi, Bronx) for $54.5M to Equality Charter.
Build-to-suit school completed 2025; holds 900 students, includes cafeterias, gym, rooftop recreation.
Equality Charter operating 3 other Bronx locations; consolidation potential unclear.
stories.summary: Azimuth Development transferred ownership of a newly completed 63,000-square-foot elementary school facility at 801 Bartholdi Street in the East Bronx to Equality Charter School for $54.5 million. The property, completed in 2025, accommodates 900 students and features two cafeterias, a gymnasium, and 6,000 square feet of rooftop recreation space. Equality Charter operates three other Bronx campuses and may consolidate operations.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Build-to-suit educational real estate and charter school consolidation do not materially affect apartment supply, demand, or capital availability. However, growing charter school investment in the East Bronx signals neighborhood revitalization and family in-migration, which could support mid-to-long-term multifamily rental demand in surrounding submarkets.

stories.title: Arc Capital Lands $29M Refi for Chapman Market in L.A.’s Koreatown
stories.excerpt: Arc Capital Partners has secured $29.3 million to refinance the Chapman Market, a nearly century-old retail and dining destination in Los Angeles’ Koreatown. Voya Investment Management provided the financing for the popular 41,241-square-foot property at 3465 West Sixth Street, also known as Chapman Plaza, along one of Koreatown’s primary commercial corridors. Arc Capital acquired the historic asset 10 years ago for $30 million, records show, and secured a $25.5 million bridge loan in 2021. The property opened in 1928 and was one of the first markets in the Western U.S. designed around the use of the automobile, according to the nonprofit L.A. Conservancy. It was designated as a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument. Chapman Market has evolved into a multi-tenant dining, retail and entertainment center with a heavy concentration of Korean food and specialty concepts. Tenants include Escala, Quarters Korean BBQ, KazuNori, Starbucks, Origin Korean BBQ, Shibuyala, Toebang Café, Danbi, Tiger Sugar Boba, BHC Chicken and Uncle Tetsu, along with private club Club HUE. Northmarq’s Joe Giordani, Alex Kane and Karl Weidell facilitated the debt along with Bryan Ley and Tim Kuruzar. “If you’ve been to this property, you know it sits at the epicenter of Koreatown’s vibrant nightlife,” Giordani said in a statement. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Arc Capital refinanced Chapman Market (Koreatown, LA) for $29.3M with Voya Investment Management.
Historic 41,241 sq ft retail/dining asset opened 1928; acquired by Arc for $30M a decade ago.
Mixed-tenant center anchored by Korean food, specialty retail, and private club; strong NOI generation.
stories.summary: Arc Capital Partners secured a $29.3 million refinance from Voya Investment Management for Chapman Market, a historic 41,241-square-foot mixed-use retail and dining property in Los Angeles' Koreatown that Arc acquired 10 years ago for $30 million. Originally completed in 1928 as one of the first automobile-oriented markets in the Western U.S., Chapman Market now operates as a multi-tenant dining and entertainment center with predominantly Korean food and specialty concepts. The refinance follows a 2021 bridge loan of $25.5 million.
stories.impact: Refinance execution on stabilized retail-anchored mixed-use asset signals continued CMBS and insurance capital (Voya) appetite for well-performing urban retail despite sector headwinds. For multifamily developers considering mixed-use components, Koreatown's demonstrated retail resilience and ethnic enclave density support ground-floor retail and entertainment inclusion in new residential projects; validates experiential retail as density value-driver in infill LA submarkets.

stories.title: C-PACE Financing is Now a Capital Stack Conversation
stories.excerpt: At the in-person Connect Apartments 2026 event in Los Angeles on Sept. 22, finance naturally will be on the agenda. With C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) financing an increasingly important element of getting deals done, the experts brought together for the “Multifamily Finance & Lending Outlook: Navigating the New Capital Stack” conversation will include Natalie Viola, SVP originations for PACE Loan Group. Viola joined PLG from CBRE Investment Management, where she served as director of debt capital markets. Here, she provides her perspective on the evolving C-PACE loan market. Q: What drew you to C-PACE financing and to PACE Loan Group (PLG) in particular? A: I was originally drawn to C-PACE because it allows me to leverage my background in highly structured capital stacks, restructuring, and in-house debt capital markets. PLG appealed to me because their platform is nimble (completely in-house team with the CEO as head of credit) and they’re willing to work through complicated structures to deliver solutions that add value; they don’t look the other way when an out-of-the-box deal comes across their desk. Q: How do C-PACE clients’ requirements differ from those of clients with whom you’ve worked in other phases of your career? Would you say those differences are smaller than they would have been a few years ago? A: The underwriting and credit fundamentals are the same, while pricing, sizing, and certainty of close remain the key differentiators. With C-PACE, it’s typically a capital stack conversation, as clients ask how it sits alongside their senior loan and what happens on a sale or refinance. Those differences are meaningfully smaller than a few years ago as the product has become more common and more senior lenders are consenting. bullets: C-PACE financing gaining prominence as structured capital stack component in multifamily deals.
PACE Loan Group hiring senior originations exec (Natalie Viola from CBRE) to scale platform.
Connect Apartments 2026 event (LA, Sept 22) will feature 'Multifamily Finance & Lending Outlook' panel.
stories.summary: C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) financing is emerging as an increasingly critical component of multifamily capital stacks. PACE Loan Group appointed Natalie Viola, formerly director of debt capital markets at CBRE Investment Management, as SVP of originations to scale its platform and navigate complex deal structures. The evolution reflects growing developer reliance on alternative capital sources to bridge cost and leverage gaps in the current rate environment.
stories.impact: C-PACE availability and platform expansion lower effective all-in borrowing costs for new multifamily development, particularly for energy-efficient projects and value-add conversions. Rising C-PACE adoption suggests developers are layering junior capital to improve returns in a higher-rate environment; monitor C-PACE program changes by state and funding availability as a key underwriting variable affecting development feasibility thresholds and project-level returns.

stories.title: CBRE Names Chris Poppell, Dawson Rinder to Mid-Atlantic Leadership Roles
stories.excerpt: CBRE has expanded its Mid-Atlantic leadership team with the addition of Chris Poppell as managing director and investor services leader for the Mid-Atlantic and Dawson Rinder as managing director and Maryland market leader. “Chris and Dawson are outstanding additions to our leadership team and reflect our continued investment in the future of our Mid-Atlantic business,” said Kyle Schoppmann, president, CBRE Mid-Atlantic. “Their experience, leadership and client focus will strengthen our ability to serve clients across the region as we continue driving growth, investing in talent and expanding our capabilities.” Poppell will help scale the firm’s investor services business across the region. Most recently, he served as director of investment real estate at George Washington University. Rinder will oversee business operations and growth strategy across the firm’s Maryland business. He most recently served as managing director and market leader of Marcus & Millichap’s Washington, D.C. office, overseeing the firm’s business across D.C., Maryland and Virginia. The post CBRE Names Chris Poppell, Dawson Rinder to Mid-Atlantic Leadership Roles appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE names Chris Poppell (managing director, investor services) and Dawson Rinder (Maryland market leader).
Poppell relocating from George Washington University real estate role; Rinder from Marcus & Millichap D.C. office.
Reflects CBRE investment in Mid-Atlantic leadership depth and regional growth ambitions.
stories.summary: CBRE expanded its Mid-Atlantic leadership team with two senior appointments: Chris Poppell as managing director and regional investor services leader, and Dawson Rinder as managing director and Maryland market leader. Poppell recently served as director of investment real estate at George Washington University, while Rinder previously led Marcus & Millichap's Washington, D.C. office overseeing D.C., Maryland, and Virginia business. The moves signal CBRE's commitment to scaling regional capabilities.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, competitive poaching of talent from Marcus & Millichap's D.C. platform and university endowment roles signals strong brokerage competition for institutional multifamily transaction flow in the Mid-Atlantic; may indicate tightening competition for deal sourcing and capital advisory services in Washington, Maryland, and Virginia markets.

stories.title: $83M Sale of Oregon Multifamily Assets Brokered by Institutional Property Advisors
stories.excerpt: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap, announced the sale of two Oregon multifamily assets, which traded for a total of $83 million. The transactions included Oak Vale, a 257-unit property in Corvallis, and the 181-unit Anjou Club in Talent. “The quality of construction and maintenance of these two properties attracts and retains the most discerning renters, and previous ownership was meticulous in their upkeep and reinvestment,” said Anthony Palladino, IPA senior director of investments. Palladino, Philip Assouad, Giovanni Napoli, Ryan Harmon, and Nick Ruggiero of IPA, in association with David Tabata, Marcus & Millichap’s broker of record in Oregon, represented the seller, Bender Equities, and procured the buyer, Verdant Development. Oak Vale is a 31-building property situated on more than 16 acres. Anjou Club was completed in 1990 and spans nearly 14 acres.“These transactions demonstrate the depth of capital seeking opportunities in established Pacific Northwest markets and investors’ continued confidence in the long-term performance of the multifamily sector,” said Andrew Leahy, national director of IPA Multifamily. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post $83M Sale of Oregon Multifamily Assets Brokered by Institutional Property Advisors appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA) brokered $83M sale of two Oregon multifamily assets.
Oak Vale (257-unit, Corvallis) and Anjou Club (181-unit, Talent) sold to Verd; Bender Equities seller.
438-unit total portfolio; 5-broker IPA team plus local Marcus & Millichap broker.
stories.summary: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a Marcus & Millichap division, brokered the $83 million sale of two Oregon multifamily properties: Oak Vale, a 257-unit asset in Corvallis, and Anjou Club, a 181-unit property in Talent, both sold by Bender Equities to buyer Verd. The brokerage team highlighted the properties' construction quality and meticulous upkeep as value drivers for attracting and retaining tenants. The dual-asset sale reflects continued institutional capital deployment in secondary Oregon markets.
stories.impact: Oregon multifamily market demonstrating sustained buyer appetite and pricing support for well-maintained secondary-market assets; sale to Verd (likely value-add or institutional buyer) suggests confidence in Corvallis and Talent rental fundamentals. For developers, signals liquidity for class-B/C hold assets and validates Oregon as accessible exit market; monitor Verd's investment thesis for market signals on preferred submarkets and value-add strategies.

stories.title: In Health Care Real Estate, Creativity Abounds — It Has To

In addition to the twin challenges of providing quality care and turning a profit while doing so, health systems are navigating regulatory pressure, accelerated project timelines and other real estate issues. During the event, experts discussed what it takes to shape the next iteration of health care infrastructure through strategies such as rethinking how funds are allocated to the best practices for revitalizing aging facilities. The day kicked off with a conversation between Vincent Grippo, senior vice president of real estate and facilities services at Northwell Health, and Mitch Green, senior vice president with AECOM Tishman. Mitch Green and Vincent Grippo. PHOTO: Greg Morris/For Commercial Observer Grippo began by sharing his story, which includes a 25-year career across several client-facing organizations. bullets: Commercial Observer National Healthcare Forum convened Sept 10 to address health system real estate evolution.
Panelists (Northwell Health, AECOM Tishman) discussed capital allocation, facility revitalization, regulatory pressure.
Focus on accelerated timelines and adaptive use strategies for aging healthcare infrastructure.
stories.summary: Commercial Observer hosted a National Healthcare Forum featuring health system executives, construction managers, and real estate advisors discussing the evolution of health care infrastructure and delivery. Speakers including Northwell Health's senior VP of real estate shared perspectives on capital planning, facility revitalization, and navigating regulatory pressure and accelerated project timelines. Healthcare real estate transformation and adaptive use strategies do not materially affect apartment supply or demand, though aging hospital facility conversions in dense urban markets could create future adaptive-use opportunities for developers (e.g., medical office to residential, mixed-use conversions); monitor for market-specific healthcare consolidation or facility closures that could unlock valuable infill redevelopment sites.

stories.title: Andreessen Horowitz to Open West Palm Office for Defense-Tech Bets
stories.excerpt: Venture capitalist behemoth Andreessen Horowitz is opening an office in West Palm Beach, Fla., which will focus on defense-tech investments. The firm, also known as a16z, signed a lease at Related Ross’ CityPlace Tower, according to a representative for the landlord, who declined to provide the size of the footprint. The office, which is scheduled to open early next year, will serve as a regional headquarters for a16z’s $1.18 billion American Dynamism fund, led by general partner Katherine Boyle, the Menlo Park, Calif.,-based firm announced. A representative for a16z did not immediately respond to a request for additional details. The transaction marks another West Palm Beach win for Stephen Ross, Related Ross’ billionaire owner, who has launched a $10 billion development spree to turn the city into a leading tech and finance hub. Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan Chase have all signed leases at Related Ross-owned office buildings since the onset of the pandemic. The lease also marks a return to South Florida for a16z. In 2022, the firm opened an office in Miami Beach to make crypto investments, only to shutter the 8,300-square-foot base two years later — and three years before the end of agreement. A16z follows another defense-tech giant, Palantir, which relocated its global headquarters from Denver to Aventura this year. Ross purchased CityPlace Tower, where a16z will be based, for $175 million in 2021, according to property records. Built in 2008 at 525 Okeechobee Boulevard, the 18-story building spans 303,519 square feet. The developer is building two more Class A office buildings after obtaining a $772 million construction package last year. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) opening West Palm Beach office at Related Ross' CityPlace Tower early 2026.
Regional HQ for $1.18B American Dynamism fund focused on defense-tech investments; led by Katherine Boyle.
Joins Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase at Related Ross properties; part of $10B development spree.
stories.summary: Andreessen Horowitz announced it will open an office at Related Ross' CityPlace Tower in West Palm Beach, Florida, scheduled to open early 2026, serving as regional headquarters for its $1.18 billion American Dynamism defense-tech fund. The lease follows a16z's 2022 South Florida office closure and marks part of Related Ross owner Stephen Ross' larger $10 billion initiative to position West Palm Beach as a leading tech and finance hub. Major financial institutions including Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, and J.P. Morgan Chase have leased Related Ross office space since the pandemic.
stories.impact: Major venture capital and defense-tech footprint in West Palm Beach signals significant professional-class employment growth and high-income talent in-migration, driving sustained multifamily rental demand in the metro. Density of financial services and tech infrastructure investment around CityPlace Tower and Related Ross properties creates flywheel effect for Class A multifamily absorption in walkable West Palm Beach submarkets; prioritize development or acquisition in neighborhoods within 1–2 miles of office concentration to capture white-collar renter demand.

stories.title: Longpoint Buys Miami-Dade Warehouse Portfolio for $195M
stories.excerpt: Longpoint Partners has dropped $195 million on a 10-building industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade County, the Boston-based private equity firm announced. The portfolio, composed of small-bay properties, spans 729,901 square feet across 41 acres. The buildings average about 73,000 square feet with clear heights ranging from 17 to 25 feet. They’re 90 percent leased to 74 tenants, each occupying an average 10,000 square feet. “This acquisition reflects the conviction and discipline that have guided our work here: acquiring functional, well-located small-bay industrial assets with a diverse tenant base in locations where new supply is difficult to create,” Dwight Angelini, co-founder and managing partner of Longpoint, said in a statement. A representative for Longpoint has yet to provide the addresses of the properties or the name of the seller. Since 2023, Longpoint Partners has been making sizable, bulk purchases of South Florida industrial properties. It has spent nearly $600 million on 51 buildings in two portfolio acquisitions. More recently in July, the firm bought three fully leased warehouses, totaling 121,579 square feet, for $39 million. Longpoint Partners also specializes in grocery-anchored retail properties. In June, it sold a 71,191-square-foot asset near Boynton Beach to Publix for $24 million. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longpoint Partners acquired 10-building industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade for $195M; 729,901 sq ft across 41 acres.
Small-bay buildings average 73k sq ft, 17–25 ft clear heights; 90% leased to 74 tenants averaging 10k sq ft each.
Longpoint spent ~$600M on 51 buildings in South Florida since 2023; targets supply-constrained micro-logistics assets.
stories.summary: Longpoint Partners, a Boston-based private equity firm, acquired a 10-building industrial portfolio in Miami-Dade County for $195 million comprising 729,901 square feet across 41 acres of small-bay properties. The buildings average approximately 73,000 square feet with clear heights ranging from 17 to 25 feet and are 90 percent leased to 74 tenants with average occupancy of 10,000 square feet each. Since 2023, Longpoint has deployed nearly $600 million acquiring 51 buildings across South Florida, targeting functional, well-located small-bay assets with diversified tenant bases in supply-constrained locations.
stories.impact: Longpoint's aggressive South Florida industrial roll-up ($600M in 24 months) reflects sustained logistics demand and land scarcity driving institutional capital toward functional, micro-logistics real estate. For multifamily developers: industrial land absorption and investor focus on Miami-Dade constrain available redevelopment/infill sites; monitor industrial portfolio valuations and lease rates as proxies for submarket land value and competitive pressure; supply-constrained small-bay markets may support higher multifamily density premiums and justify vertical mixed-use development in industrial-adjacent corridors.
